course.title.note: The interface's own messages (id.json: the draft banner, the preview page) still call the course "Digital World". Either keep the English name there and here, or change those messages to "Dunia Digital".

course.description.source: A free course with 17 lessons about AI and the digital world through social studies: where AI came from, who builds it and at what cost, how it changes daily life, and who decides how it is used.
course.description.back: A free course with 17 lessons about AI and the digital world through social studies (IPS): where AI came from, who makes it and what its price is, how AI changes daily life, and who decides how AI is used.
course.description.note: "Social studies" is "IPS", as in Our World's home page (KEY_TERMS). "At what cost" became "apa harganya" (what its price is), which can read as money only; the course means people, power and water too.

sections.0.title.note: "Thinking machines" as "mesin yang berpikir". The lessons say AI does not really think; the title echoes the old dream (Lesson 2's "Dreams of thinking machines").

sections.0.question.source: What is AI, and where did it come from?
sections.0.question.back: What is AI, and where did it come from?

sections.0.description.source: Trace how AI developed from the 1950s to today: the ideas people tried, the setbacks and successes, and what made each change possible. Then see how two of today's approaches work: a model that learns from labelled examples, and a large language model.
sections.0.description.back: Trace AI's development from the 1950s until now: the ideas people tried, the setbacks and successes, and what made each change possible. Then see how two present-day approaches work: a model that learns from labelled examples, and a large language model.

sections.1.title.source: Who builds AI, and at what cost
sections.1.title.back: Who makes AI, and what its price is
sections.1.title.note: "At what cost" as "apa harganya" (as in the course description).

sections.1.question.source: Who makes AI work, and who pays for it?
sections.1.question.back: Who makes AI work, and who bears its cost?

sections.1.description.source: Meet the people behind AI, weigh the power and water it uses, ask which languages it speaks, and see why it works better for some people than others.
sections.1.description.back: Get to know the people behind AI, weigh the electricity and water it uses, ask which languages it masters, and see why AI works better for some people than for others.

sections.2.question.source: How is AI changing work, school and community life?
sections.2.question.back: How does AI change work, school and community life?

sections.2.description.source: Look at how AI changes jobs, health, farming and school, and weigh safety against privacy when cameras can recognise faces.
sections.2.description.back: See how AI changes jobs, health, farming and school, then weigh safety and privacy when cameras can recognise faces.

sections.3.question.source: Who decides what we see, and how AI is used?
sections.3.question.back: Who decides what we see, and how AI is used?

sections.3.description.source: Check fake pictures and claims, see how feeds choose what we see, compare the rules people are making for AI, and plan an AI helper for a community.
sections.3.description.back: Check fake pictures and claims, see how feeds choose what we see, compare the rules people are making for AI, and plan an AI helper tool for a community.
sections.3.description.note: "Feed" as "linimasa" (timeline), the word Indonesian apps use; the translator of Lesson 14 should use the same (TERMS.md).

practiceOptions.3.source: I practised another way (quietly, with sign, or in writing)
practiceOptions.3.back: I practised another way (in my head, with sign language, or through writing)
